scenario.figure_or_table: Table III and Table IV (256-core Intel SCC-based 2-D chip steady-state/transient speed comparison, PACT vs HotSpot)
scenario.description: 256-core processor (2-D IC) inspired by the Intel SCC scaled to 22 nm, with a power profile from prior work (Eris et al.) chosen for the highest thermal gradient and chip temperature (hot spot power density 216.6 W/cm2). Simulated with PACT and HotSpot using the same medium-cost heat sink. Published as a speed comparison. The paper text gives no per-block floorplan coordinates or per-block powers.
scenario.architecture: 256-core 2-D processor inspired by Intel SCC (IA-32 cores) scaled to 22 nm, with a medium-cost heat spreader and heat sink
scenario.workload: Selected simulated SCC-based chip power profile from Eris et al. (DATE 2018) giving the highest thermal gradient and chip temperature
scenario.operating_point: Steady-state and transient; hot spot power density 216.6 W/cm2; grid resolution and other setup details are in Table III (not extractable from the text)

original_setup.solver: PACT, a SPICE-based parallel compact RC thermal simulator (Xyce 6.12 with OpenMPI 3.1.4). Steady-state solvers named in the paper are KLU, SuperLU and AztecOO; the transient solver is TRAP (hybrid backward Euler/trapezoidal). Compared against HotSpot (SuperLU steady-state, adaptive RK4 transient). Source: PDF pages 7-8.
original_setup.optimizer: None. The scenario is a simulator speed comparison and has no design or placement optimizer.
original_setup.controller: None. No runtime thermal controller is used in this scenario.
original_setup.benchmark: 256-core 2-D processor inspired by the Intel SCC scaled to 22 nm (IA-32 cores). The power profile comes from Eris et al. (DATE 2018) and is the one with the highest thermal gradient and chip temperature (hot spot 216.6 W/cm2). It is simulated with the same medium-cost heat spreader and heat sink in PACT and HotSpot; setup in Table III and results in Table IV, PDF page 8.

physical_mismatches.reason: The paper gives no per-block floorplan (x, y, width, height) and no per-block watts for the 256-core SCC chip. Only a hot spot power density of 216.6 W/cm2 is stated, so no complete experiment can be reconstructed. The power profile comes from prior work (Eris et al.), which is not packaged.

The scenario reports simulation speed (Table IV). Its temperature results are not available in the extractable text, so no paper thermal observable value exists for comparison. The ~90 degC maximum and ~9 degC gradient quoted on page 11 belong to the separate OpenROAD MPSoC scenario.

The original solver is a compact RC netlist solved by Xyce on an MPI cluster, with a medium-cost heat spreader and heat sink, and the grid resolution is given only in Table III. A Studio solver, package and cooling model will differ in discretization and boundary conditions, so temperatures are not directly comparable.
The scenario has no optimizer and no controller, and the power trace is a single selected profile. The original does not exercise any optimizer or controller behavior to replicate.

The paper's monolithic 3-D, liquid-microchannel and 2.5-D PNoC cases are separate scenarios and are not used. The selected case is 2-D with a conventional heat sink, so no 3-D or interposer mismatch applies to the selected scenario.

studio_assumptions: No Studio package or material assumptions are supplied in the packet, so none can be recorded as paper-derived. Any Studio default stack, materials and heat sink would differ from the paper's medium-cost heat sink.
Any placement the runner generates would be illustrative and separate from paper facts, and its temperatures must not be numerically compared to the paper.

methods.note: The PACT method is supported by text on pp. 3-8: SPICE-based compact RC netlist, Xyce 6.12 with OpenMPI 3.1.4, KLU/SuperLU/AztecOO steady-state solvers, TRAP transient solver, and a medium-cost heat sink. code.note: The only code references are the unpinned URLs github.com/peaclab/PACT (p.2 footnote 3) and OpenSTA (p.7 footnote 4). The assets list is empty, so no pinned code, commit, or script exists. A bare URL is not evidence, and the OpenSTA link does not supply SCC inputs.

parameters.note: Only the hot spot power density of 216.6 W/cm2 (p.8) is supported, and the conversion to 2,166,000 W/m2 is arithmetically correct. Table III (grid resolution, die size, heat sink spec) and Table IV were not visible in the text extraction, and no page image was supplied to verify them. There are no per-block geometry or power parameters. The 1.9x and 232x speedups are speed metrics only. The text on p.8 also states 232x for the SCC chip while the abstract and p.3 state a 186x maximum for OpenROAD designs, so these are different scenarios and must not be mixed.

config.note: There is no pinned config, floorplan, thermal, or power file (assets empty). The experiment is declared custom_2d_steady with an empty floorplan and empty power_w, so no runnable configuration exists. Table III contents are unverified because no figure or table image was supplied.

data.note: There are no floorplan block coordinates or names, and no per-block same-scenario power for the 256-core SCC chip. The power profile comes from Eris et al. (ref 20), which is not packaged. The thermal observable is null, and Table IV is unreadable. Any 2D shelf placement with constant power rows would be an illustrative assumption, not a reproduction of a published placement or transient trace. The study is a speed comparison and includes a monolithic 3D/transient/heat sink feature set (Table IV also covers the 33-layer monolithic 3D chip), so it cannot be treated as a 2D steady-state reproduction. Every floorplan block lacks power, so the check fails.

assessment.summary: The selected scenario is the 256-core Intel SCC-based 2-D chip (PACT vs HotSpot speed comparison, Table III/IV, PDF page 8). The 2D screening label is illustrative_2d_only, and the experiment kind is custom_2d_steady, which has no transient trace. Studio did NOT run: simulation status is skipped, simulation_allowed is false, and comparison_valid is false. The input gate failed because a custom experiment needs 1-128 blocks and a power_w object, and the extraction supplied an empty floorplan and no per-block powers. The scientific gate also failed and nothing is independently verified. The paper gives only a hot spot power density of 216.6 W/cm2 (2,166,000 W/m2), the Eris et al. (DATE 2018) power profile source, and speed results (max 1.9x steady-state and 232x transient speedup vs HotSpot). It reports no thermal observable with a page, unit, location, aggregation and regime, so there is no paper temperature to compare against and no Studio temperature was produced. No numerical comparison is made. Any qualitative statement is limited to this: the result would be sensitive to the package, heat sink, discretization and boundary assumptions, which were not specified for Studio. The pinned packet has no assets, so the source commit is unavailable. The linked PACT and OpenSTA repositories are not pinned and do not prove that the SCC inputs exist. No placement was generated, so no illustrative input.flp or one-row input.ptrace exists. The final verdict is gated off: this is not a replication and no exact match is claimed.
